sword.name: Sword
sword.description: An old enchanted sword. It is said to respond to correctly completed maxims, though no one has yet demonstrated this usefully.

brass-key.name: Brass key
brass-key.description: A small brass key blank labelled NOT THE PRINCESS KEY. It has potential, but not enough teeth.

lock-pattern-rubbing.name: Lock-pattern rubbing
lock-pattern-rubbing.description: A charcoal rubbing of some extremely fussy lock teeth, obtained from an East Street delivery cart.

heath-lane-key.name: Heath Lane key
heath-lane-key.description: A properly cut key made by Señor Dos' Garage. It looks smugly specific.

art.alt: The open City Gates of Gaalway at dusk.
The open City Gates of Gaalway at dusk.

text: The Princess of Gaalway has been kidnapped by the evil Mario Puzo. The King has selected you for the rescue because you were the only person near the palace who owned a sword.
It is a perfectly adequate reason to begin an adventure.

art.alt: The open City Gates of Gaalway at dusk.

text: You are standing at the City Gates of Gaalway. The gate is open, which is a surprisingly generous definition of security.
The King has given you 100 gold pieces and a sword to rescue his daughter from the evil Mario Puzo. The sword looks professionally sharp. The plan does not.

choices.label: Get so confused that you walk into the gate

art.alt: The crooked shops and bench of Low Street.

text: Low Street is named after its low buildings, low prices, and the astonishingly low expectations of its town planner.
A bench offers no useful advice, but is extremely firm about the matter. This is a side street, not the way towards Heath Lane.

art.alt: The bustling Market Street of Gaalway.

text: Market Street is busy with traders selling turnips, maps of other streets, and one very determined umbrella.

At the centre stands the Gatekeeper, wearing a helmet, a teapot, and the expression of a man interrupted during both lunch and philosophy. Beside him, a brass merchant sells keys that have not yet decided what they open.

choices.label: Ask the Gatekeeper about Mario Puzo

art.alt: A brass-key merchant in the busy Market Street of Gaalway.

text: The merchant sells you a small brass key blank for one gold piece, then returns the gold because he cannot decide where to keep the till.
‘It will open anything,’ he says, ‘once someone more technically minded tells it how.’

choices.label: Ask the Gatekeeper about Mario Puzo

art.alt: The Market Street gatekeeper with a helmet and teapot.

text: ‘Mario Puzo?’ says the Gatekeeper. ‘Terrible fellow. Keeps locking roads and calling it interior design.’

He points north. ‘Heath Lane is closed by a tiny, very important lock. A key alone will not impress it. Try East Street, then ask the fellow on Christian Street. He repairs carriages, gates, and occasionally opinions.’

choices.label: Thank him and return to the market

art.alt: A cluttered eastern street in Gaalway, with a delivery cart blocking the road.

text: A delivery cart has shed a wheel and now occupies the entire road with the authority of a small, wooden mayor.

Its driver is trying to hold the cart still while making a charcoal rubbing of the unusual lock-pattern stamped on its official axle permit. This seems an unnecessarily specific problem until you remember the Gatekeeper.

choices.label: Use the brass key to chock the runaway wheel
choices.blockedHint: The wandering wheel needs something small, firm, and metallic before anyone can work safely.

choices.label: Go to Christian Street
choices.blockedHint: The delivery cart has chosen to occupy the whole street until its wheel is made less adventurous.

art.alt: A delivery cart safely chocked on East Street in Gaalway.

text: The brass key holds the wheel just long enough for the driver to breathe, finish the rubbing, and decide you are probably an engineer by association.
‘Take this,’ she says, handing you the lock-pattern rubbing. ‘I have two, and one of them keeps judging my handwriting.’

art.alt: The workshop doorway of Señor Dos' Garage on Christian Street.

text: Christian Street is quieter than the market, apart from the reassuring clank of tools and a sign reading ‘SEÑOR DOS' GARAGE: WHEELS, WINCHES, WHIMS.’
The workshop door is open. Inside, someone is explaining the structural weaknesses of a wheel to the wheel itself.

art.alt: Christian speaking across the workbench at Señor Dos' Garage.

text: Christian looks up from a workbench crowded with gears, wheels, and a wrench that appears to be listening. ‘Welcome to Señor Dos' Garage,’ he says. ‘If it turns, sticks, or refuses to move on principle, I can at least explain why.’
You mention Heath Lane. He nods thoughtfully. ‘That lock needs a properly cut key. Bring me brass to cut and a pattern with the right teeth, and I can make it something useful.’

choices.label: Ask Christian to cut a Heath Lane key
choices.blockedHint: Christian taps the empty workbench. ‘I need brass to cut and something reliable to copy.’

art.alt: Christian offering practical advice at the workbench of Señor Dos' Garage.

text: ‘Mostly wheels,’ says Christian. ‘But gates are just wheels that have become suspicious of horizontal movement. And locks are tiny committees with teeth.’
He points to the workbench. ‘The trick is never to force a mechanism. Give it the right reason to cooperate.’

choices.label: Ask Christian to cut a Heath Lane key
choices.blockedHint: Christian taps the empty workbench. ‘I need brass to cut and something reliable to copy.’

art.alt: Christian presenting a newly cut Heath Lane key across the workshop bench.

text: Christian studies the rubbing, measures the brass key blank three times, and makes a series of tiny cuts with a tool that has more confidence than any tool should possess.
‘There,’ he says, handing you the Heath Lane key. ‘It should open the gate. If it opens a bakery instead, do bring me back a bun.’

choices.label: Thank Christian and return to Christian Street

art.alt: A tiny locked gate blocking the road to Heath Lane.

text: A petite iron gate blocks the way. Its lock is no bigger than a biscuit, though likely less crumbly. It gives the distinct impression that an ordinary key would merely offend it.

choices.label: Open the Heath Lane gate
choices.blockedHint: The tiny lock seems to be waiting for a more exact answer.

art.alt: The now-open gate on the road to Heath Lane.

text: The lock clicks open with theatrical reluctance. Beyond it lies Heath Lane—the current end of the route, and at last the proper adventure.

You have reached the immediate goal by following clues, helping a stranded cart, and obtaining a key with exactly the right amount of confidence. Mario Puzo remains at large, presumably arranging something unnecessarily complicated.

art.alt: Gaalway's harbour street, with a boat and tall masts.

text: The harbour smells of salt, rope, and an argument about haddock. A ferryman waves, then charges you a wave fee.

art.alt: The City Gates of Gaalway, shortly before an avoidable collision.

text: You become so confused that you walk directly into the gate. The gate wins decisively.
The Princess remains kidnapped. The gate has no comment.
